`בְּהְיוֹתוֹ` divided under rules 52 and 18: *when* to the preposition, *was* to the infinitive, *he* to its subject suffix.

review_notes: The verse's two cola repeat one construction; each `קוֹל` takes its own supplied *with*/*With* under rule 33 rather than one being read as distributed scope, since the Hebrew writes the noun twice.

alignments.note: *pour out* is one lexical verb with its phrasal particle, head on the verb, rule 44; the subject pronoun is the verb's under rule 17.

review_notes: Both `לִפְנֵי` phrases meet rule 30's one-rendering condition, the ASV spending a single *before* on each pair; their suffixes stand outside the fusion and take the written *him*.

alignments.note: Temporal `בְּ` before an infinitive construct takes the *When*, rule 52.
Infinitive keeps the verb with its supplied copula-auxiliary; head on the lexical verb. The margin's *fainted* was read and set aside under rule 38.

Finite verb with its auxiliary and subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb, rules 17 and 24.

Preposition.
Pronominal suffix, rule 18.

review_notes: The waw of `וְאַתָּה` is unrepresented: the ASV writes no connective before *Thou knewest*, and the explicit pronoun takes its own *Thou* under rule 20 rather than a connective being read into it.
The marginal *Or, fainted* was read and set aside; the printed *was overwhelmed* governs, rule 38.

alignments.note: Imperative.

Bare nominal with no preposition or object marker: the supplied *on* is licensed by the noun's own case-function, rule 33. `יָמִין` → *right hand* heads on *right* by rule 31's subtraction, *hand* being the generic the ASV supplies to complete the phrase; the unit is discontinuous around the supplied possessive under rule 25.
No suffix or other possessive morpheme stands in the phrase, so this supplied possessive is `added` under rule 18's closing sentence; the ASV's italic corroborates and decides nothing, rule 7.
Conjunction rendered *and*, rule 14.
Imperative.
The ASV renders this waw by *For*; the connective list is read off the ASV and is open, rule 14.
Existential `אַיִן` takes the supplied presentative frame and heads on the negation word, rule 50.
The recasting promotes the preposition's object to the direct object of *knoweth*, leaving the preposition no English word, rule 40.
The suffix takes the English pronoun that realizes it, rule 40's first sentence with rule 18.
Anarthrous participle used substantivally takes the noun phrase the ASV supplies — the generic *man* with its relative — and heads on the word carrying the lexeme, rule 46.

Anarthrous participle with the generic *man* the ASV supplies to make it an English noun phrase, headed on the lexeme-bearing word, rule 46.
Preposition rendered *for*.
Noun.
Possessive suffix, rule 18.

review_notes: Head of `יָמִין` → *right hand* taken on *right* under rule 31; the competing reading heads on *hand* as the class noun, but the ASV does not write *hand* alone for this word here and *right* is what carries the lexeme.

The italic *my* of *my right hand* is `added` because no possessive morpheme stands in the phrase; the two `אַיִן` clauses are aligned separately on what each actually writes, the first with the presentative frame and the second without.

review_notes: `בְּאֶרֶץ הַחַיִּים` → *in the land of the living* is the arthrous case of rule 29: the ASV writes a *the* before each noun, so the article takes the one standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one.

review_notes: `הַקְשִׁיבָה` is divided under rule 32: the imperative takes *Attend* and the paragogic *he* is unrepresented.
`דַלּוֹתִי` → *I am brought very low* heads on *low*; the competing reading heads on *brought*, but *brought* alone brings anything and *low* is what carries the lexeme, rule 44.

alignments.note: `הוֹצִיא` → *Bring ... out*: one lexical verb with its phrasal particle, head on the verb under rule 44, discontinuous around the object under rule 25. The competing reading gives *out of* whole to the `מִן` under rule 24; the ASV's word order, which puts *out* after the object, is what decided it.
Paragogic *he* has no English realization, rule 32.
Ablative preposition; the *out* beside it is the verb's phrasal particle, as above.

The infinitive takes its supplied subject and modal, rule 52; `יָדָה` → *give thanks* is rule 44's light verb plus complement, headed on *thanks*.
The English verb reaches its object through *unto*, and the object marker is the morpheme that takes that word, rule 16.

review_notes: The marginal *Or, crown themselves because of me* was read and set aside; the printed *shall compass me about* governs, rule 38, so `בִּי` is unrepresented with its suffix taking *me*.

*out* of *Bring my soul out of prison* was given to the verb rather than to `מִן`, the ASV writing it after the object as an English phrasal particle; the alternative reading `מִן` → *out of* is recorded in that unit's note.
